articles.title: Checking a temporarily suspended bus stop
articles.summary: A stop may be skipped even while the wider bus route continues. An offline record can help a household identify what to confirm before setting out.

visual.alt: Conceptual sequence diagram for checking a temporarily suspended bus stop: Find notice; Check access; Reconfirm. These are planning prompts, not a live map, verified service status or permission to enter restricted areas.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid only; check current operator or authority information.

sections.title: Understand the change
paragraphs: Read the operator's dated notice and identify the exact stop name, direction and route number; a stop on the opposite side of the road may have different arrangements.

Record the stated alternative boarding point only if the operator has identified it. Do not assume the next physical stop is served, step into the carriageway to flag a bus, or treat an old screenshot as a current instruction.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: Compare the alternative with the traveller's walking distance, step-free access and need for a safe crossing. Ask the operator about an accessible arrangement when the suggested point is unsuitable.
Keep a short paper note of the route, stop identifier and operator contact. Check current notices again before travelling, since temporary arrangements can change.

articles.title: Preparing for a temporary tram stop relocation
articles.summary: A temporary tram boarding point can change the path between the street and the platform, particularly for people who need step-free access.

visual.alt: Conceptual route diagram for preparing for a temporary tram stop relocation: Usual stop; New stop; Check access. These are planning prompts, not a live map, verified service status or permission to enter restricted areas.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid only; check current operator or authority information.

sections.title: Understand the change
paragraphs: Distinguish a stop relocation from a line closure. Write down the line, travel direction, new stop name and any date range shown in the operator's notice.
Look for specific information about lifts, ramps, crossings and interchange distance rather than assuming a relocated stop has the same accessibility features as the usual one.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: Create a small comparison card with the normal stop, operator-named replacement and a question mark beside anything not confirmed. The card is a memory aid, not a route authorisation.

Check the operator's latest information before departure and follow staff instructions and site signs. If the replacement is inaccessible, contact the operator for an appropriate alternative rather than improvising a trackside route.

articles.title: Planning around an unavailable cycle-hire docking station
articles.summary: A cycle-hire journey depends on both collecting and returning a bicycle, and a docking station can be unavailable without the entire scheme stopping.

visual.alt: Conceptual checklist diagram for planning around an unavailable cycle-hire docking station: Return plan; Backup trip; Support. These are planning prompts, not a live map, verified service status or permission to enter restricted areas.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid only; check current operator or authority information.

sections.title: Understand the change
paragraphs: Before relying on a shared cycle, note the scheme's official help contact, return rules and the location of other legitimate docking areas.
Do not infer that a dock is working from an old map or an offline screenshot. A payment or app outage may also prevent unlocking or ending a hire.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: Allow for a non-cycle fallback when arrival time matters. Record the operator's instructions for a failed return rather than leaving a bicycle unsecured or assuming a rental has ended.

If a hire cannot be closed correctly, keep the transaction or bicycle reference privately and use the operator's support channel when available. Avoid publishing account identifiers in public reports.

articles.title: Preparing when station luggage lockers are unavailable
articles.summary: A station storage closure can disrupt a journey involving heavy bags, accessibility needs or an onward appointment.

visual.alt: Conceptual shelves diagram for preparing when station luggage lockers are unavailable: Claim ticket; Provider contact; Plan B. These are planning prompts, not a live map, verified service status or permission to enter restricted areas.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid only; check current operator or authority information.

sections.title: Understand the change
paragraphs: Check whether the notice concerns self-service lockers, a staffed left-luggage desk or both. They can have different opening hours and acceptance rules.
Write down the operator's official enquiry channel and any published collection arrangements for items already stored. Do not assume a closure notice permits access to a restricted area.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: Plan to carry less luggage or arrange an authorised alternative before travel. Consider whether the alternative is accessible and whether its operating hours match the journey.
Keep claim receipts and item identifiers in a private place, not on a shared noticeboard. Follow the storage provider's instructions for retrieving belongings and confirm changes before travelling.

articles.title: Keeping travel options when a transport app account is unavailable
articles.summary: An app login problem is different from a service cancellation, but it can prevent access to tickets or travel records.

visual.alt: Conceptual sequence diagram for keeping travel options when a transport app account is unavailable: Ticket rules; Fallback; Check charges. These are planning prompts, not a live map, verified service status or permission to enter restricted areas.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid only; check current operator or authority information.

sections.title: Understand the change
paragraphs: Identify which journeys depend on an app login, a mobile ticket or a payment card. Some ticket products are not valid as screenshots, so never assume an image is acceptable proof of travel.

Before a journey, check the operator's permitted offline ticket access and customer-support routes. Keep non-secret booking references separately where useful, without saving passwords or authentication codes on a shared card.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: If the account cannot be opened, use an operator-approved alternative purchase or validation method rather than bypassing barriers or relying on an unaccepted screenshot.
Record the issue and any support reference for later follow-up. After access returns, check for duplicate purchases or charges before making a repeat booking.

articles.title: Understanding a temporary accessible parking bay suspension
articles.summary: A temporary parking suspension can remove a familiar accessible arrival point even when the destination remains open.

visual.alt: Conceptual checklist diagram for understanding a temporary accessible parking bay suspension: Bay notice; Alternative; Step-free. These are planning prompts, not a live map, verified service status or permission to enter restricted areas.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid only; check current operator or authority information.

sections.title: Understand the change
paragraphs: Read the authority's posted notice for the precise bay, dates and restrictions. An accessible parking permit does not automatically override a signed temporary suspension.
Identify whether the destination has an authorised alternative drop-off or parking arrangement. Avoid assuming that nearby loading bays, footways or closed roads are lawful substitutes.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: Record the destination's accessibility contact and ask about step-free access from the alternative arrival point, including kerbs and crossing points.
Recheck official signs on arrival. If an essential visit becomes inaccessible, contact the venue or responsible authority to discuss options instead of parking in a restricted or unsafe place.

articles.title: Making an offline record of public-service helpline hours
articles.summary: A saved telephone number is less useful without knowing which team it reaches and whether it is an ordinary-hours contact.

visual.alt: Conceptual checklist diagram for making an offline record of public-service helpline hours: Service; Hours; Checked. These are planning prompts, not a live map, verified service status or permission to enter restricted areas.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid only; check current operator or authority information.

sections.title: Understand the change
paragraphs: For each essential public service, record its official name, purpose, published number and the date the details were checked. Keep emergency contact information distinct from general enquiries.
Do not invent an out-of-hours service or assume a call centre is staffed around the clock. A printed number may change, so label the record as an offline reference rather than a live directory.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: Use a readable two-column paper format: service and contact details. Add an alternative accessible contact method only if the organisation officially offers it.
Review entries periodically and after a provider change. Keep personal case numbers separate from any household card that visitors might see.

articles.title: Checking accessibility after a rail platform change
articles.summary: A platform alteration may change the step-free route through a station even if the booked train is still running.

visual.alt: Conceptual route diagram for checking accessibility after a rail platform change: Train details; Step-free route; Ask staff. These are planning prompts, not a live map, verified service status or permission to enter restricted areas.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid only; check current operator or authority information.

sections.title: Understand the change
paragraphs: Treat a platform shown on an old ticket or screenshot as provisional. Platform allocations can change, and a platform number alone does not establish a step-free path.

Check the rail operator or station's current information about accessible routes and any assistance arrangements. Avoid entering staff-only passages, crossing tracks or using an unauthorised shortcut.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: Keep the train service, station contact and booked assistance details together for quick reference, without exposing personal identifiers in a public note.
Allow time to speak with authorised staff when a changed platform makes the planned route difficult. Follow current announcements and signs rather than relying solely on the offline note.
